test_cases.title: Login form reflows without horizontal scroll at 320px viewport width
test_cases.when: the viewport is resized to 320px width
test_cases.then: the form remains fully usable with no horizontal scrolling, consistent with existing .stats-grid responsive breakpoints

attempts.reason: round-1 finding: tautological assertion: jsdom reports form.scrollWidth=0 and form.clientWidth=0 (no real layout engine), so `expect(form.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(form.clientWidth || form.scrollWidth)` reduces to 0<=0 and passes unconditionally regardless of actual CSS/responsive behavior — does not genuinely verify no-horizontal-scroll at 320px
round-1: same tautology confirmed on retry — not a flake, a structural test-authoring defect

last_run.revalidation_note: Round-2 re-validation (post round-1 fix). Test at frontend/src/components/__tests__/LoginForm.test.jsx:70-88 replaces the jsdom scrollWidth/clientWidth tautology with a structural, non-tautological check: (1) no LoginForm-rendered element carries a fixed inline px width >320px, (2) the shared `.form-input`/`.form-select` CSS rule in frontend/src/styles/index.css (spot-checked at lines 1117-1126, confirmed `width: 100%`, no fixed px width/min-width) is relative. Independently mutated the CSS rule to `width: 500px` and re-ran the test in isolation: it FAILED as expected (`expected '\n  width: 500px...' to match /width:\s*100%/`), confirming the assertion is genuinely load-bearing, not vacuous. CSS mutation reverted and diff-verified identical to original before final full-suite run. Classified PASS (proxy/structural coverage, not pixel-perfect rendered-viewport measurement — same honest-disclosure treatment as AUTH-04 TC-02/TC-10/TC-14; disclosed as AF-05 in docs/features/AUTH-01/FLAGS.md).
